tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.

name: claude-adaptive-thinking-disabled
purpose: D-H3, CONFIG GATE OFF (the shipped value): `claude.enableAdaptiveThinking: false` must make a claude-(opus|sonnet)-4-6 model take the NON-adaptive thinking path, so pinned sends `thinking:{type:'enabled',budget_tokens:<n>}`, raises max_tokens to the 1024-token minimum and drops temperature/top_p/top_k (chat-completions.js:112 module-load read, :260 `(enableAdaptiveThinking && /^claude-(opus-4-6|sonnet-4-6)/)`, :372-390 non-adaptive branch). DISCRIMINATING BECAUSE: the request body carries `reasoning_effort:'high'`, so the two config values take visibly different shapes at the provider -- with the gate OFF the recorded body must contain a `budget_tokens` thinking member, and an implementation that hardcodes the adaptive default (the pre-fix Go behaviour) emits `thinking:{type:'adaptive'}` + `output_config:{effort:'high'}` instead, which the bodySha256 comparison fails on. The request is identical to claude-adaptive-thinking-enabled; only the config line differs, so the PAIR is what proves the config is read rather than the model string.
